display.title: Episode 276: Judge for a Day, Chapter 1
display.summary_short: Preparing for Shavuos: Hashem creates the world anew every moment, two sisters recite the Shema, an honest butcher is accused of theft, and Mitzvah Time begins learning about Havdalah.
display.summary_long: Broadcast in the middle of Sefirah 5747, as listeners prepare for Shavuos by improving their midos. Uncle Yossi teaches the first Mishnah of Pirkei Avos, chapter 5: the world was created with ten sayings. Unlike a carpenter who only shapes wood, Hashem creates something from nothing, and must keep creating it every moment, just as a bulb shines only while the current flows; so we owe Him our very life and should thank Him with Torah and better behavior. Two sisters from a Brooklyn girls' school recite the Shema and one of the Twelve Pesukim. Story time begins 'Judge for a Day': bright, kind Leibel hears that Berel the butcher, known to all as honest, is accused by sly Ivan the tailor of stealing 365 gold coins, found wrapped in a red handkerchief under Berel's floorboard. Berel says Tehillim, and Leibel prays for a way to help. On Mitzvah Time, Uncle Yossi begins the laws of Havdalah: its meaning, its time after the stars come out, and the Havdalah kit, with a phone-quiz prize offered. He closes with the unity of the Jewish people at Har Sinai.
display.lesson: Hashem keeps the whole world in existence every moment; we show our thanks by learning Torah and improving our midos.
